paper.passageHint: Passage comes from your exegetical paper. Change it if you want to reorient the sermon.
paper.exegesisHint: This section is a summary of your paper. If you want deeper analysis or the Greek Tutor, regenerate it from this step.
paper.homileticsHint: Approach derived from the '{{tone}}' tone you chose. Pick another approach or regenerate options.
paper.draftHint: Draft pre-loaded from the paper. Refine via chat, edit it directly, or publish.

faculty.headline: Pre-populated from your Faculty session: {{title}}
faculty.passageHint: Passage comes from the outline you approved in Faculty. Edit it if you want to reorient the sermon.
faculty.exegesisHint: This exegesis is a short summary from the Faculty outline. If you want deeper canonical analysis with the Greek Tutor and your library references, regenerate it from this step.
faculty.homileticsHint: Points come from the approved outline and the pastoral personalization you added. Pick another approach or regenerate options.
faculty.draftHint: Draft generated from your Faculty session. Refine via chat, edit it directly, or publish.

citationVerification.descVerifying: Checking that author-attributed quotes are actually present in the source material.
citationVerification.descIssues_one: Found {{count}} citation that probably isn't in the source material. Fabricated pulpit citations destroy credibility — review and fix before publishing.
citationVerification.descIssues_other: Found {{count}} citations that probably aren't in the source material. Fabricated pulpit citations destroy credibility — review and fix before publishing.
citationVerification.descClean_one: Checked {{count}} author-attributed citation and it appears in the source material. Safe to publish.
citationVerification.descClean_other: Checked {{count}} author-attributed citations and all appear in the source material. Safe to publish.
citationVerification.descNoCitations: The sermon contains no author-attributed quotes. Only Scripture is cited — nothing to verify.
citationVerification.descLibraryNarrative: Your citations are narrative attributions anchored to your library, verifiable by clicking each marker.
citationVerification.descUnavailable: This sermon is not linked to an exegetical paper or Faculty session, so there's no source material to verify citations against. If your sermon cites authors, double-check them manually.

inProgress.title: Sermons in Progress
inProgress.subtitle: Continue working on your saved sermons.

passage.title: Select a Biblical Passage
passage.descWithTitle: What biblical text will you use to develop this sermon?
passage.descDefault: The base text you will use to develop your sermon.
passage.comingSoonDesc: Based on your sermon title and description, we'll be able to suggest relevant passages.

empty: No sermons found matching your search.

exegesis.title: Exegetical Study
exegesis.subtitle: Analyze the original text and define the biblical basis of your sermon.
exegesis.refiningStatus: Refining section. Use chat to make changes.
exegesis.defaultStatus: Click 'Refine' to expand a section, or use chat for general queries.
exegesis.whatIsDesc: Exegesis is the critical analysis of the biblical text in its original language, considering historical, literary, and cultural context.

errors.invalidArray: Model did not return a valid array

homiletics.title: Homiletical Analysis
homiletics.subtitle: Develop the structure and purpose of your sermon based on the exegesis.
homiletics.phase2Sub: 🎨 Phase 2: Generating proposition and detailed outline
homiletics.typesDesc: Thematic, Pastoral, Theological, Apologetic, Evangelistic and Narrative. Each with its own purpose.
homiletics.audienceDesc: Each approach is optimized for a specific audience. Choose the one that best connects with your congregation.
homiletics.developmentDesc: Once selected, we will generate a homiletical proposition and outline specifically tuned to the tone and purpose of your chosen approach.
homiletics.tipText: There is no "correct" approach. Choose the one that resonates best with your church's current needs.
homiletics.subtitle2: Build the bridge to contemporary application.
homiletics.readyToGenerate: Ready to generate your homiletical proposal
homiletics.readyDesc: Based on your exegetical analysis, I will create 4-5 different homiletical approaches for you to choose the most appropriate one.
homiletics.proposalDesc: Review and refine the content using the chat
homiletics.whatIsDesc: Homiletics is the art of building the bridge between the biblical text and the contemporary audience, transforming eternal truth into practical application.

success.previewsGenerated: {{count}} approaches generated. Select the best one for your context.
success.developed: Approach fully developed. Review and refine!

errors.readonlySection: This section is read-only and cannot be edited directly
errors.refineShape: Could not refine "{{section}}": the assistant returned an unexpected shape. Your content is untouched — try again.

regenerateConfirm.title: Regenerate Homiletical Study?
regenerateConfirm.description: This action will restart the entire homiletical process. New approaches will be generated and you'll lose the current selection and manual refinements.

contract.title: Proposition and outline
contract.subtitle: They are one contract: the points inherit the proposition's noun and call to action. Edit them together.
contract.secondPersonVerb: The verb is in second person. Your propositions use first person plural: the preacher stands with the congregation, not outside it.
contract.disclaimer: It flags what's missing; you decide. It doesn't block.
contract.applicationPlaceholder: This point's application — how it lands on the hearer

directive.intro: What you write here is yours: the assistant never rewrites it, and the draft treats it as an instruction.
directive.staleDescription: This description was written for this point's previous passage. Ask the assistant to rewrite it if it no longer fits.
directive.emphasisLabel: Emphasis — the angle of this point
directive.emphasisPlaceholder: e.g. God speaks, but his word is not without purpose: he speaks to direct his people.
directive.notePlaceholder: e.g. “paid the fare”: the Hebrew does not say it was his personal fare; it personifies the ship.

selection.title: Choose your sermon approach
selection.desc_one: There is {{count}} way to preach this passage.
selection.desc_other: There are {{count}} ways to preach this passage. Compare them and choose the one that best serves your church.
selection.thesisNote: Every approach preaches this idea: the route changes, not the thesis.
selection.regenerateConfirmDesc: The approaches in this list are replaced. If you had already chosen one, the choice is lost.

drafting.title: Sermon Draft
drafting.subtitle: Your study and outline are ready. Choose how to write the sermon.
drafting.readyToGenerate: Ready to generate your complete sermon
drafting.readyDesc: I will create a complete sermon with introduction, point development, illustrations, conclusion, and call to action.
drafting.refiningStatus: Refining section. Use chat to make changes.
drafting.defaultStatus: Click 'Refine' to expand a section, or use chat for general queries.
drafting.finalDraftDesc: This is the last step. I will generate a complete and structured sermon based on your exegesis and homiletical analysis.
drafting.loadingSub: This may take a few moments

regenerateConfirm.title: Rebuild the draft from scratch?
regenerateConfirm.description: A new draft will be written from your proposition and outline, replacing the current one.
regenerateConfirm.workshopDescription: The new draft is written from your proposition and outline, not from what you decided in the Workshop. If what you want is a draft updated with your decisions, assemble it again from the Workshop. Your decisions are never deleted.
regenerateConfirm.keepVersion: Save the current draft to history
regenerateConfirm.keepVersionHint: You will be able to go back to it section by section. Uncheck it if you would rather not pile up versions.

versions.assembledWithBackup: Draft built. The previous one is in the history.

afterGenerateList: Refine the introduction, points and conclusion by talking with the assistant
Regenerate a point you're not convinced by, without redoing the sermon
Go back to any earlier version of each section
Publish the sermon when it's ready

callToActionParts: 1 to 3 concrete steps for this week
skeleton.title: How your sermon will be shaped

elements.sectionJob: Place the listener in the world of the text: what its first hearers knew, and what they feared.
elements.myIdeaPlaceholder: Write the idea you want this section to carry. One or two sentences — the prose comes later.
elements.proposeFailed: Couldn't fetch suggestions. Your own idea is still the main path — write it above.
elements.decidedTitle: What you decided for this section
elements.onePerLine: One idea per line. Write several and add them all at once.

shape.propia: The ideas in this section are yours.
shape.mixta: This section mixes your own ideas with ones you chose.
shape.seleccionada: This section was built by choosing. Over time, more of it will come from you.

elements.flipKind: Switch between your own idea and a topic to cover
elements.unsupported: No direct support in the text
elements.oneIdeaHint: Write it whole, as you will tell it. Line breaks don't split it — it's one image.

quotes.sinFuentes: Your library has nothing on this point. Write the quote yourself, or leave it without one — better than quoting something off-point.
quotes.sinCoincidencias: There is material in your library, but none supports what this point claims.
quotes.falló: Couldn't search your library. Try again.
quotes.multiVoiceAdvice: A point rests on one voice, not several stacked up: if this point needs two voices, it may be a sign it wants to be split. Your call.

keyWords.propose: Bring the ones from my study
keyWords.sinPalabras: Your study recorded no key words for this passage.

elements.replacedPrevious: This section holds a single decision: the new one replaced the previous.

exposition.label: Point {{n}} — exposition
exposition.job: Say what the text says and why it matters. This is the point's content.

illustration.label: Point {{n}} — illustration
illustration.job: Make the idea visible with something the congregation recognizes.

application.label: Point {{n}} — application
application.job: What changes Monday morning if this is true.

recap.label: Conclusion — recap
recap.job: Gather the thread of the points without repeating them.

callToAction.label: Conclusion — call
callToAction.job: Ask for a concrete response, not a feeling.

openingIllustration.label: Introduction — opening illustration
openingIllustration.job: Open a question the sermon will answer.
openingIllustration.heading: Opening Illustration

bookOverview.label: Introduction — the book at a glance
bookOverview.job: Place the passage within the whole book.
bookOverview.heading: The Book at a Glance

historicalContext.label: Introduction — historical context
historicalContext.job: Place the listener in the world of the text: what its first hearers knew, and what they feared.
historicalContext.heading: Historical Context

title.label: Title
title.job: Name the sermon. Your proposition is below to guide you, but a title is a different thing: it does not assert, it names.
title.context: Your proposition, to help you think it through:

verbatim.label: The sermon title
verbatim.placeholder: Write it exactly as you want it to appear.

sections.coveredNote: Already yours, from the study or the outline. Nothing to decide here.

pointProposition.label: Point {{n}} — proposition
pointProposition.job: One sentence summing up what you want them to see in this point. It is to the point what the homiletical proposition is to the sermon: the concepts it holds are the ones you then unpack.

verbatim.label: This point's proposition
verbatim.placeholder: One sentence: what you want them to see in this point.

sections.pointPropositionContext: Your proposition for this point — this section's ideas unpack it:

currentConnection.label: Introduction — current connection
currentConnection.job: Bridge the world of the text and your congregation's, without preaching the point yet.
currentConnection.heading: Current Connection

sermonProposition.label: Introduction — homiletical proposition
sermonProposition.job: The sermon's thesis, as you wrote it in Homiletics. It lands at the end of the introduction.
sermonProposition.heading: Homiletical Proposition

verbatim.label: The sermon's proposition
verbatim.placeholder: The thesis the whole sermon holds up.

transition.label: Point {{n}} — transition
transition.job: Pick the proposition back up and announce the next point. Derived from the outline — nothing to decide.

sections.keyWordsContext: The words you studied, with what you said about each:
sections.transitionContext: This composes itself from your outline. Above you can add the phrase you use to move to the next point:

authorityQuote.label: Point {{n}} — authority quote
authorityQuote.job: A voice that backs what you just expounded. Only if you have a verifiable one: an invented quote in the pulpit destroys credibility.

keyWords.label: Point {{n}} — key words
keyWords.job: The words from your study this point uses. Decide which belong here; they enter the draft as you leave them.

prose.label: This section's prose
prose.failed: Couldn't write it. Your decisions are still saved.
prose.emptyNoDecisions: First decide what goes in this section. The prose is written from that.
prose.emptyReady: You've decided. Press “Write this section” to draft it.
prose.propositionOpens: In the sermon, your proposition opens this section in your exact words. Here you write only what unpacks it.

assemble.missing: {{count}} sections would come out EMPTY, starting with “{{first}}”. You can build anyway.

study.title: Your study of {{passage}}
study.readOnlyNote: Read-only. The study is edited in its own step; here it feeds your decisions.

paths.heading: Two paths to your draft
paths.subheading: Both start from your study and your outline. The difference is who decides the ideas.
paths.workshopDesc: You decide section by section — your ideas, your study’s words, your quotes — and the assistant writes from what you decided.
paths.generateDesc: The assistant writes the whole sermon from your study and your outline. Useful when time is short: you can refine it in the workshop, and the draft will be marked as generated.

provenance.generated: Generated — refine it in the workshop

drafting.emptyDraftTitle: You have not assembled the draft yet
drafting.emptyDraftDesc: Decide the sections in the Workshop and press “Assemble draft”, or generate the full sermon from the band above.

pastoralContext.title: Pastoral context (optional)
pastoralContext.hint: Funeral, wedding, crisis, emphasis, anecdotes… the more you tell it, the more the sermon fits.
pastoralContext.intro: None of this gets filed away: it goes into the sermon being written. Your illustrations are used as you wrote them, and the draft takes your congregation's language.
pastoralContext.languageEverydayHint: Explains theological terms as it uses them. Greek and Hebrew only where they help. Illustrations from daily life.
pastoralContext.languageTechnicalHint: Greek, Hebrew and morphology where the text calls for it. Assumes systematic categories. Established Reformed authors.
pastoralContext.situationalPlaceholder: e.g. It will be preached at a funeral service, or after a crisis in the community…
pastoralContext.congregationPlaceholder: e.g. 80 people, Reformed, medium-high theological level
pastoralContext.emphasisPlaceholder: What do you want the congregation to feel, understand, or do when the sermon ends?
pastoralContext.illustrationsPlaceholder: Personal anecdotes, congregation stories, or testimonies you want to include…
pastoralContext.notesPlaceholder: Loose ideas, arguments you want to develop, particular emphases…

gate.completeStudy: Complete the {{count}} study steps before moving on to the draft.

paperReference.title: From your paper “{{paperTitle}}” · {{count}} for this step
paperReference.disclaimer: This is what you already established in your paper. It is here to consult: what you write in this step has to be yours. In word studies, tap a word to adapt its explanation into your study.

citations.ownTranslation: Our translation · the original is one click away
citations.translateFailed: Couldn't translate. The original is still above.

insightStep.title: Insight
insightStep.subtitle: Your pastoral voice, without the assistant. This is what the sermon will develop.

help.label: What goes in each field? See quick guide
help.exampleCentralIdea: “Christ freed us from condemnation through the perfect work of the Spirit in our mortal flesh.”
help.exampleDoxology: “Worship the God whose righteousness accomplished in Christ what our flesh never could. Live evangelical freedom with joyful holiness, not legalistic resignation.”
help.intro: This step is your pastoral voice. There is no assistant here: the sermon is built on what YOU write on this screen.
help.centralIdea: Central idea: one sentence that sums up the sermon. It will appear as written in the final draft.
help.observations: Observations: 3 or more truths the text affirms. Each becomes a section of the sermon.
help.openQuestion: Open question: the question your sermon answers.
help.anecdote: Pastoral anecdote: a story or example that connects the text with real life.
help.doxology: Doxological application: what worship, holy living or faithful ministry this sermon should lead to.

noAssistant.title: No assistant in this step
noAssistant.body: The draft is built on your exact words on this screen. If you paste them from another tool, we log it for your own review: not to judge you, but so you know how much of your sermon is truly yours.
noAssistant.pastes_one: {{count}} paste event logged in this session.
noAssistant.pastes_other: {{count}} paste events logged in this session.

centralIdea.label: Central idea (1 sentence, at least {{min}} characters)
centralIdea.hint: It will appear as written in your final sermon. Be precise.

tripwire.title: Review this claim before moving on

observations.label: Observations
observations.hint: What the text affirms, demands, rules out. Each at least {{minChars}} characters; each becomes a section of the sermon.
observations.placeholder: Observation {{n}}: a truth the text affirms.

openQuestion.label: Open question (at least {{min}} characters)
openQuestion.hint: The question your sermon will help answer.

anecdote.label: Pastoral anecdote (at least {{min}} characters)
anecdote.hint: A story, example or illustration that connects the text with real life.

doxology.label: Doxological application (at least {{min}} characters)
doxology.hint: What worship, holy living or faithful ministry should this sermon lead to?
